name: Minimum Possible LCM
description: You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$. Your problem is to find such pair of indices $$$i, j$$$ ($$$1 \le i \lt j \le n$$$) that $$$lcm(a_i, a_j)$$$ is minimum possible. $$$lcm(x, y)$$$ is the least common multiple of $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ (minimum positive number such that both $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$ are divisors of this number).
input_specification: The first line of the input contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^6$$$) — the number of elements in $$$a$$$. The second line of the input contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^7$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the $$$i$$$-th element of $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Print two integers $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ ($$$1 \le i \lt j \le n$$$) such that the value of $$$lcm(a_i, a_j)$$$ is minimum among all valid pairs $$$i, j$$$. If there are multiple answers, you can print any.
approach_summary: Apply Euclidean Algorithm paradigm under the Number Theory framework. Exploit problem invariants to reduce state space and achieve optimal complexity.
